question.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ -1 & 3 \\ 2 & -3\end{aligned}],\,B=\{{u}_{1},{u}_{2}\}=\{[\begin{aligned}\frac{\sqrt{6}}{6} \\ -\frac{\sqrt{6}}{6} \\ \frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]\}
$$

Consider the subspace $\text{Col}(A)$ and an **orthonormal** basis $B$ of $\text{Col}(A),$ where $A$ and $B$ are given above. Given that $B$ is derived from $\text{Col}(A)$ using the Gram-Schmidt process, what is the value of $|a|+|b|+|c|?$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that $\text{Col}(A)$ is the span of the columns of $A.$  

First, let's denote

$\,$ ${a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 3 \\ -3\end{aligned}].$ 

We proceed to find an orthogonal basis using the Gram-Schmidt process, as follows.

**Step 1**: We set ${v}_{1}={a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

**Step 2**: Next, we find ${v}_{2}$, by using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{2} & ={a}_{2}-\frac{{a}_{2}\cdot {v}_{1}}{{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}}{v}_{1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the formula for ${v}_{2}$ in our case gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{2} & ={a}_{2}-\frac{(-3)\cdot 1+3\cdot (-1)+(-3)\cdot 2}{{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{2}^{2}}{v}_{1} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 3 \\ -3\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we normalize each vector to get an orthonormal basis:

- ${u}_{1}=\frac{{v}_{1}}{‖{v}_{1}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{2}^{2}}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{\sqrt{6}}{6} \\ -\frac{\sqrt{6}}{6} \\ \frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}\end{aligned}].$

- ${u}_{2}=\frac{{v}_{2}}{‖{v}_{2}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3} \\ \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3} \\ \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, $B=\{{v}_{1},{v}_{2}\}=\{[\begin{aligned}\frac{\sqrt{6}}{6} \\ -\frac{\sqrt{6}}{6} \\ \frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3} \\ \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3} \\ \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\end{aligned}]\}$ is an orthonormal basis for $\text{Col}(A).$

Finally, $a=-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3},$ $b=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3},$ $c=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}$ and  

$$
|a|+|b|+|c|=|-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}|+|\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}|+|\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}|=\sqrt{3}.
$$
